text: Benjamin Joseph Allen, born on January 5, 1947, is an American academic who served as president of the University of Northern Iowa (UNI) from 2006 to 2013. On March 24, 2017, it was announced that Allen would begin serving as interim president of Iowa State University on May 9, following the departure of former president Steven Leath, who accepted a position at Auburn University. Allen earned a Bachelor of Science in business economics from Indiana University Bloomington in 1969, a Master of Arts in economics from the University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign in 1973, and a Ph.D. in economics from the same institution in 1974. He taught at Washington State University from 1974 to 1979 and served as a Brookings Economic Policy Fellow in the Office of Transportation Regulatory Policy at the U.S. Department of Transportation from 1976 to 1977. Allen joined the faculty of Iowa State University in 1979. During the 1986–87 academic year, he was the Visiting McKinley Professor of Economics and Public Utilities at the University of Illinois, and from 1990 to 1991, he held the Oren Harris Chair in Transportation at the University of Arkansas. From 1984 to 1988 and again from 1991 to 2002, Allen was a professor at Iowa State in the departments of economics and transportation. He chaired the Iowa State University Department of Transportation and Logistics from 1984 to 1988 and served as dean of the Iowa State University College of Business from 1994 to 2000. From 2002 to 2006, Allen was vice president for academic affairs and provost at Iowa State University, succeeding Rollin C. Richmond, who later became president of Humboldt State University. At Iowa State, he was named the first University Distinguished Professor in Business. Allen was named the ninth president of the University of Northern Iowa on April 28, 2006, and assumed office on June 5, 2006. In 2007, he was appointed by the American Association of State Colleges and Universities and the National Association of State Universities and Land-Grant Colleges to the Presidential Advisory Committee for the National Commission of University Accountability. Under his leadership, UNI established priorities to increase student achievement in undergraduate programs and provide statewide leadership in Pre-K through 12 education, including its lead role in the Iowa Mathematics and Science Education Partnership with Iowa State University and the University of Iowa. During his tenure, the ninth U.S. Secretary of Education, Arne Duncan, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Michelle Obama visited the campus and delivered speeches. Allen is co-chair of the Institute for Tomorrow's Workforce, a non-profit educational foundation aimed at preparing all Iowa learners for the 21st century global marketplace. He is an ex-officio board member of the Iowa Department of Economic Development and co-chairs the education subcommittee of the Iowa Business Council, which includes education and business executives committed to enhancing Iowa's economic vitality. A strong supporter of the local community, Allen is a member of the executive committee of the Greater Cedar Valley Alliance and a director of Heartland Express Company. Allen was diagnosed with prostate cancer on November 15, 2010, and took a leave of absence beginning on February 7, 2011. Provost Gloria Gibson served as interim president during his absence. Allen underwent a routine procedure and fully recovered. On February 29, 2012, the Teacher Education Faculty at UNI voted 15-1 (with one abstention) to express no confidence in President Allen, Provost Gloria Gibson, and the Iowa Board of Regents, protesting the decision-making process surrounding President Allen's recommendation to close the Malcolm Price Laboratory School and Northern University High School, effective June 30, 2012. On March 2, 2012, the university faculty voted 197-53 in support of a motion of no confidence in President Allen, citing a lack of faculty consultation in the closure decision and related academic program cuts. On March 15, 2012, the American Association of University Professors (AAUP) announced it would investigate allegations that the UNI administration violated academic governance rules in making budget cuts and firing faculty, with the possibility of formal censure. On October 24, 2012, Allen released an online statement regarding a student in a psychology course at UNI who, as a member of the Iowa National Guard, could not attend an exam due to military obligations. The student spoke with professor Cathy DeSoto, who indicated she would review the university's policy on military service and apply the standard missed-class policy. The student later filed a standard grievance as recommended by DeSoto. In his statement, Allen expressed strong disagreement with the professor's decision and emphasized that the university had been working with the student to ensure no penalty would be imposed for military service. Allen released the statement before speaking with DeSoto, and no penalty was or has been applied to the student. However, the statement triggered angry calls and emails to DeSoto and her family, as well as vandalism of her car, requiring a police escort. A letter from AAUP President Rudy Fichtenbaum criticized Allen's handling of the case, stating that the media response, which unfairly and falsely portrayed DeSoto's actions, was a direct result of Allen's premature and provocative press release, and that it led to threatening communications to DeSoto and her family.
